# 1. Objective

The previous rotor-noise model is a *descriptive* two-component spectral fit:
per line, a narrow core plus broad shoulders, with the two areas historically
named "coherent" and "incoherent". The revised model replaces that
interpretation with a physical mechanism — one latent shaft state per rotor,
shared by all of its harmonics, plus independent per-harmonic phase diffusion —
and the campaign asks one question about it:

> Does synthetic audio rendered from the revised model move a **frozen,
> real-trained** rotor-speed tracker's error closer to the error it makes on
> **real** audio, without damaging the rigs and regimes the current model
> already serves?

"Closer" is a measured gap closure, defined in §2. The gap being closed is the
positive difference between the frozen tracker's error on real recordings and
its error on the best existing synthetic arm; that gap is **calibrated first**,
before any candidate is evaluated, because a gap indistinguishable from zero
makes the whole comparison meaningless (§7).

Two things the objective deliberately is **not**. It is not "the best-scoring
model": the deliverable is the **simplest** model and fitting procedure that
satisfies all frozen criteria (§4). And it is not a proof that the synthetic
trajectory reference is physical ground truth: the primary score is **reference
agreement** against a shared raw telemetry array (§3).

# 2. Frozen success criteria

These are frozen. They are not softened, not loosely restated, and no threshold
is moved to let a model through.

## 2.1 DREGON — cruise only

The scorer is the frozen real-trained HPPNet L2 tracker, `hppnet_l2_r2_s0`,
*best* checkpoint, with the **actual checkpoint digest pinned in the manifest**
and recorded in the saved output. It scores PIT MAE on matched **real** and on
**baseline/candidate synthetic** audio. The positive real-vs-synthetic gap is
calibrated first. The point target is

$$
E_{\text{new}} \le E_{\text{real}}
+ 0.70\left(E_{\text{best synth}} - E_{\text{real}}\right),
$$

that is, a closure of **at least 30 %** of the real–synthetic gap, and the
**one-sided 95 % cluster interval must exclude no improvement**.

::: {.callout-warning}
## What a cluster is — and what the 12-row probes are not

Clusters are **independently recorded trajectory sessions**: the five no-source
room2 cruise recordings. They are explicitly **not** different physical
aircraft, not different channels, not different analysis windows, and not
different render seeds. Resampling is **matched and paired at recording
level**, on concrete recording/window identity — never by position and never by
modulo.

The existing 12-row probes are **not** 12 independent recordings. Any interval
computed as if they were is invalid.
:::

There is **no standby or ramp acceptance for DREGON**, and DREGON standby/ramp
need not be fitted at all. Held-out predictive supports use a **4 s common
length** across the five recordings.

## 2.2 Michael's rig — fixed-recording gate on FLY124

The population-level 95 % criterion is **explicitly waived by the user**,
because there is only one held-out eight-channel recording, FLY124. The gate is
a fixed-recording gate, and **equal regime weighting applies to the primary MAE
itself**, not to per-regime ratios. Form, separately for the baseline arm and
the candidate arm,

$$
E_{\text{rig}}=\tfrac13\left(
E_{\text{standby}}+E_{\text{ramp}}+E_{\text{cruise}}
\right),
$$

and then require

$$
\frac{E_{\text{rig,new}}}{E_{\text{rig,best}}}\le 1.05 .
$$

::: {.callout-warning}
## Do not average the three per-regime ratios

$(r_{\text{standby}}+r_{\text{ramp}}+r_{\text{cruise}})/3$ with
$r=E_{\text{new}}/E_{\text{base}}$ per regime is **explicitly rejected**. That
construction gives a tiny standby MAE disproportionate leverage and admits
near-zero denominators. Where an earlier shorthand said "equally weighted
three-regime ratio", it means **the ratio of equally weighted MAEs**, exactly
as written above.

**Every regime and its own ratio are still reported separately**, as
diagnostics. The gate is the single aggregate ratio.
:::

:::: {.callout-warning}
## Score the declared regime support, not the whole window

Each regime MAE is computed **only** on the outputs whose times lie inside that
regime's **pre-registered raw-telemetry support**. This is not a formality: the
Michael ramp can be **shorter than an 8 s context window**. Standby and cruise
are likewise scored on their own **declared support**.

**Regime definitions are fixed and selected before any candidate.** Regime
boundaries are never inferred from a candidate, and never from a refined or
posterior track. The ramp regime on FLY124 is **one** event starting at
approximately 31.18 s, scored inside an 8 s context that starts at 27.68 s. Do
not confuse the event with its context, and do not manufacture independent
ramps.

**Standby training envelope.** The old fit's exact standby start on FLY125 is
unknown; the conservative whole-event training envelope is **[1.78, 15.28] s**.

The regime masks and the scored times are retained as **provenance** in the
saved record, so a reader can check which samples entered which regime's MAE.
::::

Any block uncertainty is **conditional on FLY124** and is never an
across-recording population-95 claim. Fitting is on **FLY125**; **FLY124 stays
held out** for predictive checks. A frozen tracker having seen FLY125 is
**provenance**, not automatic invalidity, for matched instrument calibration;
no new airframes are demanded.

## 2.3 The separate spectral and LTAS gates

Evaluated separately from the tracker MAE, and never merged with it:

- an **overlap-aware held-out composite improvement** gate on the frozen
  composite risk
  $\mathcal{L}_c=\sum_i a_i\left[I_i/M_i+\log M_i\right]$ — positive
  overlap-exposure weights $a_i$ normalized per unique audio duration, fixed
  band 30–7900 Hz, fixed mics, existing 16 kHz convention, periodic Hann,
  NFFT 16384, hop 1024 (64 ms). Exposure is tied to the **actual analysis-frame
  supports and cadence**, not to clip spans: at NFFT 16384 with hop 1024 the
  1.024 s analysis frames overlap 16-fold, and weighting whole clips alone
  would leave every frame inside a clip at weight 1. **Duplicate identical
  observation windows split exposure**, keyed on `(recording, absolute frame
  centre, window/NFFT)`: duplicating an **analysis frame** — not merely a whole
  clip — must leave the score and the effective exposure unchanged, never
  double the evidence. This is the invariant most likely to break in an
  implementation. A fixed hop is a decision-risk setting and must never be
  presented as exact information content.
- a **baseline-calibrated LTAS** gate, stated on **absolute-level LTAS
  error**. There is **no arm-specific peak or band normalization**; a
  relative-shape LTAS may be reported as a **secondary diagnostic** only. If
  any unit-mean periodogram scaling is used, the scale is derived **once from
  the real clip** and the **same** scale is applied to **all** models and
  arms. **Never** normalize a synthetic arm independently: per-arm
  normalization would let an arm launder a level error into an apparent shape
  match. The examined render path does not preserve fitted absolute levels
  through its RMS-normalising wrapper (head of this document); that is a
  pending item of the frozen protocol, and this gate cannot mean anything
  until it is resolved.

The composite risk is valid as a **mean-prediction composite risk under
arbitrary dependence**, because $E[\mathcal L_i]=M_i^{*}/M_i+\log M_i$ is
uniquely minimized at $M_i=M_i^{*}$. It is **not** a joint NLL, **not**
evidence, **not** a posterior, and **not** an independent term count. Cellwise
Hessians and nominal frame counts cannot supply uncertainty. **No percentage
NLL** is reported, ever. The fit objective is divided by one frozen scalar
**composite temperature** $T$, defined below; any prior weight is likewise
calibrated separately on frozen planted/baseline data and then frozen before
any candidate is fitted.

::::: {.callout-note}
## The frozen composite temperature $T$

Calibrated in **one direction only**: a scalar **log-power gain** $\eta$ on the
model mean, $M_i\mapsto M_i e^{\eta}$, evaluated on the **untempered actual fit
risk** — not the per-unique-second normalized reporting form above. For a
baseline predictive draw $b$ with periodogram $I_b$,

$$
U_b=\sum_i a_i\left(1-\frac{I_{b,i}}{M_i}\right),
\qquad
H=\sum_i a_i,
\qquad
J=\operatorname{Var}_b\!\left(U_b\right),
\qquad
\boxed{\,T=J/H\,},
$$

with $\operatorname{Var}_b$ the **sample** variance over the frozen baseline
predictive draws; the fitted objective is $\mathcal L/T$ plus **one** OU prior.
$U_b$ is the gradient of the composite risk in the gain direction and $H$ its
expected curvature there, so $T=J/H$ is an ordinary **sandwich** correction
along that one direction.

- **Same weights as the fit.** $U_b$, $H$ and $J$ use the **same analysis
  exposure weights $a_i$ and the same mic and bin weights as the fit
  objective**, never the per-unique-second normalized reporting $\mathcal L_c$.
  Exposure bookkeeping and the fit temperature are **different knobs**.
- **Scope.** A **scalar gain-direction sandwich calibration** only: not
  all-parameter posterior coverage, it does not make the composite a
  likelihood, and it supplies **no** posterior curvature or uncertainty for any
  other parameter.
- **Determinism.** One **fixed master seed**; the Monte Carlo **draw count and
  the draw supports are preregistered** and frozen in the manifest (§8) before
  any candidate runs.
- **Failure rule.** A **non-positive or non-finite $J$ is a calibration
  failure**: the instrument fails loudly and must **not** fall back to a default
  or to $T=1$, exactly as a manifest lacking its threshold calibration fails
  loudly rather than defaulting to something permissive.
- **Frozen before candidates**, on frozen baseline predictive draws, and never
  retuned after seeing candidate results.

**Guarded-v2 baseline calibration is frozen.** Job
`revised-phase-round2-v2--82591d` produced
`results/revised_phase/baseline_v2/calibration.json`. The v2 split preserves
five DREGON room2 cruise recordings, 4 s held-out supports, and the symmetric
1.024 s window/filter guard; three metadata-only early-valid-window repairs were
applied before any candidate outcome. The v1 split is invalid for candidate
judgement because its baseline prepare path lacked that guard. C2 was not
refitted for v2: the same C2 training exports were reused and rescored under the
corrected split.

The v2 baseline recalibrated only the three DREGON measurements touched by the
guarded split. Temperature calibration, family selection and Michael's rig
numbers are unchanged. On DREGON cruise the real tracker error is
$1.2187080817581784$ rev/s and the baseline synthetic error is
$2.1877858830655468$ rev/s, so the 30 % gap-closure target is
$1.897062542673336$ rev/s. The mean positive gap is
$0.9690778013073683$ rev/s; its one-sided lower bound is
$0.830218608973161$ rev/s. The old v1 target near $1.669$ rev/s is historical,
not current. The DREGON LTAS tolerance is $0.05595793956082849$ dB. For
Michael's rig, $T=15.214066879865468$, with per-regime baseline MAEs standby
$0.3171026880710335$, ramp $8.007098121439082$, cruise
$0.7557833849952398$ rev/s, giving an equal-regime-mean of
$3.026661398168452$ rev/s and a point candidate maximum of

Full derivation and the interpretation of $U_b$ and $H$:
`docs/explainers/bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd` §6.2.4.
:::::

Uncertainty comes only from the **DREGON whole-recording paired bootstrap**
(five clustered units) and from **explicitly conditional contiguous-block
variation on FLY124**.

:::: {.callout-note}
## The initial gate forms, frozen before any candidate

- **DREGON composite:** paired mean $\Delta$composite $<0$ **and** the upper
  one-sided 95 % bound $<0$.
- **DREGON LTAS:** point non-regression, plus a
  **baseline-variability-calibrated tolerance** for the uncertainty allowance.
- **Michael's rig:** composite and LTAS non-regression tolerances,
  **conditional on FLY124**, calibrated on baseline data **before** any
  candidate is evaluated.

The exact **null-variation calibration rule** behind those tolerances is frozen
before candidates run and is a manifest item (§8): the instrument reads the
calibration from the frozen manifest and **fails loudly if the manifest lacks
it**, rather than defaulting to something permissive. Tolerances are never
tuned after seeing candidate results (§8).
::::

## 2.4 Both rigs: what the score means

- The **primary MAE uses the raw telemetry reference shared by all arms** — one
  array, real arm, baseline synthetic arm and every candidate synthetic arm,
  reported as **reference agreement** and never as proven ground truth. The HPP
  target stays raw even when a DREGON candidate is conditioned on `rps_refined`.
- The renderer's **realized physical shaft RPS** label supplies a
  **diagnostic** MAE only. It is never a gate and never the primary target.
- **Refined tracks may condition a DREGON candidate** in C4 because they are an
  already-published acoustic proxy. They are not a scoring reference, not an
  independent truth claim and not a way to ease the HPP gate. A better held-out
  fit says only that these labels are better supported under this model.
- Comparing older inferred carrier corrections with the existing refined tracks
  is **diagnostic only**: refined tracks are not ground truth, disagreement is
  not automatic failure, and the abandoned recovery path is not evidence for or
  against saved carrier paths.
- Training a tracker on synthetic and testing it on real is **out of scope**.

::: {.callout-note}
## The target semantics are a human convention, frozen before comparison

Mathematics separates the exogenous raw reference trajectory from the
renderer's realized physical shaft speed. It cannot decide which of them the
frozen tracker's existing MAE convention is *intended* to call its target. That
choice is an unavoidable human convention and is frozen in the manifest before
any arm is scored. Switching the primary target to the realized label would
answer a **different** supervised-task question — even though the realized
label is the physically exact render label.
:::

## 2.5 Held-out prediction versus conditional reconstruction

Primary held-out predictive synthesis uses the **declared supplied carrier**:
raw for Michael's, raw or published `rps_refined` for the two DREGON C4 arms.
It uses no fitted clip/population frequency bias, no learned delay, no
corrections inferred from held-out audio and no MAP shaft path taken from
held-out audio. Held-out prediction is the **marginal** branch of the spectral
expectation, evaluated with **moving atoms**: the supplied carrier trajectory is
integrated inside every finite window, on ramp support exactly as on cruise
support. The stationary window-correlation kernel is admissible **only** on
genuinely constant-speed bench cells, never as a slowly-varying shortcut for
held-out prediction (`bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd` §6.2.1). Held-out
guards include complete window/filter support — a disjoint contiguous support
with a guard of at least one window/filter length — so that no raw-sample
support leaks.

# 4. Selection rule

- The final deliverable is the **simplest model AND fitting procedure** that
  satisfies **all** frozen criteria — **not** the best-scoring candidate.
- Start simple. Add exactly **one** scientifically motivated complexity, and
  only when a **named** acceptance criterion has actually failed.
- If a candidate passes early, **preserve its full export, config and
  evidence**, then spend the remaining allowed rounds **simplifying**: one
  change per remaining round — remove a component, tie a component, or simplify
  the optimizer.
- **Failed simplifications never erase a passing incumbent.**
- **Thresholds are never moved to let a simpler model through.**
- Selection compares: explicit stochastic mechanisms, independent parameter
  blocks and degrees of freedom, latent states, and inference
  stages/approximations. Favour exact transitions, explicit finite-window
  kernels, and ordinary well-understood optimization. Avoid unproved structured
  filtering tricks, new particle machinery, arbitrary composite sub-objectives
  and per-harmonic free diffusion unless simpler forms measurably fail a
  criterion.
- Report **conceptual complexity** alongside the numerical scores and the
  runtime. Runtime matters, but a faster **opaque** approximation is not
  automatically simpler mathematically.

# 5. Current candidate methods: C2 and C3 failed overall, C4 in progress

## 5.1 What C2 keeps from the family

Per rig $g$ (Michael's rig, DREGON, bench), clip $c$, rotor $r$:

$$
f_{\text{actual},r}(t)=f_{\text{raw},r}(t-\delta_r)+b_{c,r}+\nu_r(t)/(2\pi),
$$

$$
d\nu_r=-\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\nu_r\,dt
+\sqrt{2\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}\sigma_g^2}\,dW_r,
\qquad
d\theta_r=\nu_r\,dt,
\qquad
d\epsilon_{rk}=\sqrt{2D_g}\,dW_{rk},
$$

with $\lambda_{\mathrm{ref}}=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ fixed for every rig as an
explicit **reference correlation-time assumption**, not as measured controller
physics. $\sigma_g$ and $D_g$ remain fitted positive rig parameters. The
renderer and finite-window atoms are the same shared-carrier family as C1: one
OU shaft state shared by all harmonics of a rotor, one scalar source-side
diffusion $D_g$ shared across orders and microphones, raw telemetry plus delay
and per-clip bias, no tonebank/noise split, no second carrier spline, no EM,
no particle method, no Kalman filter and no new stochastic mechanism.

The marginal fit cannot identify shared causal motion by itself. C2 therefore
exports the method as `fit_method="marginal_then_carrier"`,
`lambda_source="fixed_reference"` and
`shared_phase_evidence="not_identified_by_marginal_score"`; moment functions are
diagnostics, not production hyperparameter initializers.

## 5.2 The C2 fitting procedure

1. **Stage 1: marginal global fit.** Optimize the training marginal expected
   periodogram by ordinary Adam / quasi-MAP. Fit $\sigma_g$, $D_g$, existing
   power/floor/speed-law parameters, clip bias terms and the population bias.
   The integrated OU contribution is included once through the marginal mean;
   state innovations are integrated out and no unused state-path prior energy
   is added. The fixed reference $\lambda$ removes the unidentifiable timescale
   degree of freedom.
2. **Stage 2: frozen-global carrier diagnostic.** Freeze Stage 1 globals,
   including $\lambda$, $\sigma$, $D$, powers, floor and population bias. Then
   fit the per-clip bias plus the time-resolved $\theta/\nu$ path as a
   conditional MAP diagnostic under one exact OU state prior. The independent
   residual phase enters only through the conditional kernel
   $\exp(-D|\tau|)$. Stage 2 carrier tracks are training diagnostics and are
   never used to form held-out predictive atoms.
3. Keep Stage 1's predictive population bias distinct from Stage 2's diagnostic
   clip bias in the export. The two stage objectives are not summed as Bayesian
   evidence, and their values are not compared as exact likelihoods.

**Implemented schedule:** Stage 1 Adam 120 iterations at learning rate 0.1;
Stage 2 carrier Adam 40 iterations at learning rate 0.05; one frame batch per
clip; harmonic chunk 8; state grid 500 Hz; seed 0; work audio 64 kHz, analysis
16 kHz; NFFT 16384, hop 1024.

## 5.3 C3 result and carrier diagnostics

C3 kept the C2 physical model and the guarded-v2 protocol fixed. It added no new
Gaussian state, per-order diffusion, second floor family, refined-label
initialization, permanent power floors, changed metric weights or changed
thresholds. It tested one fitting hypothesis: C2's Stage 1 may have initialized
the harmonic comb too close to the floor.

The algorithmic delta was intentionally narrow:

1. estimate the floor per clip and per frequency using the existing floor-basis
   convention, then aggregate in linear physical power with the declared speed
   normalization;
2. initialize each harmonic from local **band excess power** around the moving
   raw carrier, integrating signed $(I-F)\,df$ before applying a modest
   noise-supported seed floor;
3. fit Stage 1 with active orders 16, 48 and then full-$K$, for 40, 40 and 120
   Adam iterations respectively, initializing newly admitted orders from the
   cached band-energy profile instead of resetting the already fitted orders;
4. restore full-$K$ before export, prediction and rendering; Stage 2 remains the
   same 40-iteration carrier diagnostic.

The C3 scorecard failed overall because all three DREGON gates failed. It still
created a useful partial Michael's incumbent: Michael's primary ratio
$0.625700145902331$, composite upper bound $-6881.751360910363$ nats/s and LTAS
upper bound $-0.0585890125868509$ dB all pass their frozen gates. The partial
incumbent's export digest is
`22ba6cf29edb687f43d178403e4e710c9d49e6993cfc7a6ca438b5666f3274fc`.

Small-array carrier diagnostics are stored in
`../revised-phase-preflight/results/revised_phase/carrier_diagnostics/`. They
use the reconstruction
$f_{\mathrm{model}}=f_{\mathrm{raw}}+\mathrm{diagnostic\_bias}_{Hz}+\nu_{Hz}$,
where $\nu_{Hz}$ is already in hertz; refined sidecars are anchored by
`ft + audio_t_start`; and C2/C3 are compared on shared coverage with fixed rotor
IDs and no PIT. These diagnostics are not validation. The refined reference is
diagnostic-only, and Michael's generator passing does **not** validate the
inferred real carrier paths.

Aggregated C3 diagnostics: DREGON cruise model-minus-raw MAE is
$2.462446$ Hz, model-minus-refined MAE is $2.200515$ Hz and dynamic standard
deviation is $0.643403$ Hz. Michael's C3 cruise values are $1.380027$ Hz,
$1.384311$ Hz and $1.668539$ Hz. The median centered correction correlations
are near zero (DREGON $-0.022$, Michael's $-0.008$), but these diagnostics do
not statistically prove independence. The larger raw distance is not, by
itself, tracker-error worsening because raw telemetry is the shared scoring
reference, not ground truth for real carrier paths.

## 5.4 C4 fixed-carrier experiment now in progress

C4 is an experiment under implementation, not trained, not scored and not an
accepted default. It keeps the same stochastic phase family but removes carrier
recovery from the fit. The deterministic nominal carrier is supplied and fixed:

$$
f_{r}^{\mathrm{nom}}(t)\in\{f_{r}^{\mathrm{raw}}(t),
 f_{r}^{\mathrm{refined}}(t)\},
\qquad
\phi_{rk}(t)=k\,2\pi\int_0^t f_{r}^{\mathrm{nom}}(s)\,ds
+k\theta_r+\epsilon_{rk}.
$$

For the implemented C4 estimator, $\theta_r$ is an initial phase / renderer
phase convention, not a recovered time-varying carrier-correction trajectory.
Set every clip and population frequency bias to zero and fit no additional
learned delay. Stochastic shared phase broadening remains **prior-marginalized**
in the expected spectrum; it is not estimated as a physical carrier correction
path. Renderer draws may still contain stochastic phase-frequency perturbations,
so "fixed carrier" means the supplied nominal track is fixed, not that every
sampled phase derivative exactly equals telemetry.

DREGON has two arms: `Draw`, conditioned on raw labels, and `Dref`, conditioned
on the published `rps_refined` labels. The two arms differ only in that supplied
carrier input. Both use the same C3 global warm start and reset only DREGON's
initial $D$ to $2\pi\cdot13.07=82.1212319648372$. Michael's has one raw arm,
warmed from C3 globals but with fixed raw carrier and zero bias. For all arms,
$\lambda=6\,\mathrm{s}^{-1}$ remains fixed; $\sigma$, $D$, profile/floor/speed
laws and microphone parameters are fit; all orders ($K=130$ for DREGON,
$K=230$ for Michael's) are active from the start.

The objective is one full-training marginal composite risk divided by the
frozen $T$ plus existing global priors. It has **no** OU innovation MAP prior
and no state-path optimization. The optimizer is deterministic PyTorch LBFGS
with strong Wolfe line search, `max_iter=20`, `max_eval=30`, `history_size=10`.
Closure traces are function evaluations and need not be monotone; the accepted
iterate is the object to compare. This is a local optimizer, not a global convex
fit, not exact joint likelihood, and not causal identification.
## 5.4 Historical C1, retained as rejected evidence

C1 used the off-diagonal moment estimator to freeze $\lambda_g$ and
$\sigma_g$ and initialize $D_g$ before a single conditional spectral MAP. That
estimator was repaired in code, but the honest planted preflight
`python-e25ee9` rejected the scientific route: it failed recovery at true
$\lambda/\sigma=6/6$ and the real near-coincident four-rotor support lacked
isolated moment cells. Those moment functions remain useful diagnostics and
algebra checks; they are no longer production hyperparameter initializers.

## 5.4 Multi-regime identifiability

One joint model **per rig**, not independent per-regime vectors. Michael's rig
gets one parameter law covering standby, ramp and cruise, trained on FLY125,
with one recording-level gain shared across regimes; a zero-mean per-clip
nuisance alone does **not** fix slope confounding unless it is orthogonal to
log-speed. Start from the existing power speed law and the shared recording
gain, and let log-speed dependence of the dynamics in **only** where the data
identify it. DREGON is **cruise only**. Do not mix physical rigs or bench cells
into flight data. Finite-record bias and slow-OU confounding are **reported**,
never "fixed" by adding a second free path.

# 6. Correctness checks required before belief

The canonical list, with its derivations, is §9 of
`docs/explainers/bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd`. In summary, and all
required before any fitted number is believed:

1. Exact integrated-OU planted covariance against the known covariance,
   including the near-zero $\lambda\Delta$ limit, with correlated
   $\theta$/$\nu$ increments from **one shared state**.
2. Shaft-only, independent-only and combined planted phase covariance; the $k$
   loading and order-normalised differences; biased-carrier plus bias/OU
   ambiguity **reported**, including the deliberate two-path Hessian
   gauge-direction check.
3. Conditional zero-posterior-covariance removes the OU broadening while the
   marginal prediction remains correct; $D=0$ MAP-path recovery; $\theta=0$
   scalar-$D$ recovery.
4. Pure tone and planted chirp finite-window power, including fractional bins,
   the floor and the phase units.
5. The subwindow-oscillation finite-window line, and **state-grid convergence**
   as $\Delta_{\text{state}}$ shrinks at fixed STFT hop and window.
6. Overlap duplicates create no exposure and no information; no held-out
   raw-sample support leakage.
7. The generated physical RPS integrates to the shared phase, excludes
   $\epsilon$, and has the same timeline and length as the audio after
   resampling.
8. Near-crossing behaviour is tested on the **continuously summed spectral
   components that share the same $\theta$**, together with the companion
   harmonics of both rotors: no nearest-bin classification, no forced
   unidentifiable allocation, and missing/weak-order gates declared
   beforehand. A crossing check on **joint complex observations** is reserved
   for a future candidate that actually implements that likelihood (the
   optional complex state-space / $\epsilon$-latent stack); C2 fits a marginal
   expected-periodogram composite and a separate frozen-global conditional
   carrier diagnostic, so that check does not apply to it.
9. Finite parameter and device gradients.
10. Only if a sparse method is ever introduced: small-$K$ sparse against a
    dense reference on objective value and recovery — with **no** exact-$O(K)$
    assertion.

Only a genuinely uncertain behavioural risk earns a retained regression test.

# 7. Evidence policy

- **Every number carries its scope and provenance**: which rig, which
  recording, which fit, which export or date, and laptop versus cluster. No
  number appears in this document that was not read from a source with that
  provenance attached.
- **No fabricated results.** No invented percentage, p-value, runtime or
  citation. C2 and C3 are completed scientific failures overall; C3's Michael's
  arm is historical fixed-candidate evidence only, and no overall passing bundle
  exists.
- Inherited measured results are **descriptive baselines**, cited to their
  source document or export — see `docs/experiments/stochastic-fit.md` and the
  two explainers.
- Machine evidence is produced by

  ```
  python scripts/stochastic_fit_revised_eval.py --manifest <frozen-manifest> --check
  ```

  which saves the underlying metrics **and** the gate decisions, and **exits
  non-zero on unmet gates**. Metrics are exact identity and full precision,
  paired on concrete recording/window identity.
- **Old exports are rescored**, never refitted, under an identical observation
  and renderer protocol, using their **stated** covariance and their **actual
  exported units**. A smoothed observed periodogram is not a model prediction.
- **Do not convert previously rounded or median numbers into new intervals.**
  Use baseline variability and paired whole-recording data, recomputed.
- Because the benchmark selection is **adaptive over up to eight rounds**, the
  bootstrap intervals the instrument produces are **decision/uncertainty
  summaries, not fresh-unseen confirmation**. That caveat travels as a field in
  the saved metrics record, not only in prose.
- Verified remote proof to date: `bash-1a1663` on commit `b11c613b45e7` passed
  115 tests with 2 skipped in 41.88 s on CPU; `bash-060c82` on commit
  `4632edd383e1` (V100 16 GB, K230, R4M8) confirmed 13/13 finite forward and
  backward gradients, 10.260 s cold wall time and 3.929 GB peak allocation. The
  cold wall time is not a steady fit cost. Round 1 C1 is rejected by honest
  planted preflight `python-e25ee9`; the earlier `python-c049cf` pass was an
  invalid scalar-zero fixture. Round 2 C2 core is implemented in `08b8ef3c` and
  integrated here as `635fa919`; remote proof
  `revised-phase-round2-pro-db69c3` passed 39 tests with 2 skipped in 56.72 s.
  Round 3 C3 is evaluated by
  `revised-phase-c3-eval-733d43/results/revised_phase/c3/eval_v2/` and failed
  overall while passing every Michael's generator gate. Round 4 C4 fixed-carrier
  fitting is under implementation and has not been trained or scored. The
  earlier alternating carrier-recovery preflight was abandoned before any remote
  fit. **Three of eight scientific rounds have concluded; no overall candidate
  has passed and no overall incumbent exists.**
- A successful end additionally requires: updated `.qmd` sources, rendered
  `.html`, **actual browser visual verification**, this campaign document, and
  the machine evidence above.

# 8. Freeze manifest contents

Before any candidate fit, the manifest freezes:

- the exact datasets and their pins;
- the train / calibration / held-out **waveform supports**, with the
  window/filter-length guard;
- seed and draw identities;
- the frozen tracker **checkpoint hash**;
- the **baseline export hash**;
- the score conventions (band, mics, window, NFFT, hop, weighting,
  normalization);
- the **threshold calibration**, including the exact **null-variation
  calibration rule** of §2.3 — both read from the manifest, with a loud
  failure if either is absent, rather than a permissive default;
- the **composite temperature $T$ and its calibration inputs** of §2.3 — the
  master seed, the Monte Carlo draw count, the draw supports and the resulting
  $T$ — frozen before any candidate fit, with a non-positive or non-finite $J$
  failing loudly rather than defaulting to $T=1$;
- the concrete check command of §7.

Tolerances are **never** tuned after seeing candidate results. The instrument
is built so that a tolerance cannot be retro-fitted.

# 9. Data supports and provenance

**DREGON.** The primary cohort is exactly the five **no-source room2 cruise**
recordings; they are the training/calibration pool and the five clustered
units. Disjoint remaining cruise supports are the predictive evaluation, behind
a window-support guard, using a **4 s common length** across the five
recordings; if a recording cannot supply the required support, that is
**reported** — never padded, repeated or cycled. All ten DREGON flights have
cruise. Room1 free-flight is **held out** from HPPNet; room1 noise-only may be
a separately reported transfer diagnostic only. Do not add room1
speech/whitenoise recordings to the noise-only primary gate.

**Michael's rig.** Training on **FLY125**, covering standby, ramp and cruise
under one joint parameter law. **FLY124 is held out** for predictive checks,
and every uncertainty statement about it is conditional on that single
recording.

**Bench.** An **optional planted/physical diagnostic only** — not an extra
reported scientific candidate arm, and never mixed into flight data. The bench
has no telemetry: its carrier is the audio-estimated comb rate.

::: {.callout-warning}
## There is no measured ramp fit

The current **per-regime standby and cruise exports remain the descriptive best
baseline**, and **no measured ramp fit exists**. A ramp baseline must **not** be
invented, and per-window winners must **not** be silently chosen: the baseline
family choice is made on calibration supports only and then frozen as **one**
global choice per rig/regime, with the ramp extrapolation rule stated
explicitly and labelled as an extrapolation of the current model.

Existing baseline results are **frozen, not deleted** — including the refit on
refined labels `results/S2/cruise_8clip_refined.json` (fitted `k_half`
1.73-3.27, as recorded in
`docs/explainers/bench-fit-revised-phase-model.qmd` §15).
:::

# 10. Stop / escalate conditions

Stop and escalate if:

- the DREGON real–synthetic gap is **indistinguishable from zero**;
- the required **real coverage is absent**;
- the **independent DREGON recordings are insufficient**;
- unapproved **scope or risk** appears;
- **material ambiguity** is unresolved;
- or **8 candidates fail**.

# 11. Ownership

| Owner | Files |
|---|---|
| Candidate implementation | `src/experiments/stochastic_fit/revised_phase.py` (and, if genuinely needed, one cohesive sibling module), `scripts/stochastic_fit_revised.py`, `tests/experiments/test_stochastic_fit_revised_phase.py` |
| Baseline / evaluation | `scripts/stochastic_fit_revised_eval.py`, the narrowly needed evaluation and render-AA helpers in `src/experiments/stochastic_fit/`, their tests, `docs/revised-phase-baseline-proposals.md` |
| Documentation | the four rendered documents listed at the head of this file, including `docs/explainers/rotor-noise-fit.qmd` |
| Integration | the integration owner commits scoped changes after the ownership boundary; the documentation writer does not commit |

No concurrent edits to the same files. Existing frames, clips and rig
conventions are reused; no new frameworks. The real-clip decimator, raw data,
refined labels, checkpoints and dependency locks are out of scope for every
worker.
